newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat falls on profit-taking, forecast rain.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat falls on profit-taking, forecast rain.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures fell on Friday as profit-taking wiped out some of the gains of earlier in the week after predictions of rain.
Market leader January 1998 traded down by A$9.00 a tonne to A$193.00 on 34 lots sold.
Settlement prices were also down virtually across the board, mostly by about A$8.00 a tonne. The nearby September 1997 contract's settlement price fell by A$13.50 to A$201.00.
Ed Scamps of Elders Risk Management said profit-taking emerged after private weather forecasters predicted rain in grains-growing areas in the next 10 days.
"(But) it's not over yet," Scamps said.
Forecast rain, if it arrived, would only partly assist, leaving growers still in a bad situation, he said.
Problems confronting growers in southern New South Wales and in Victoria had been compounded by severe frost, he said.
